questions.scenario: Your society is facing a big debate about stray dogs in the compound. How do you step in?

options.text: I go down every evening to personally feed the dogs and take them to the vet if they are hurt.
I listen patiently to the terrified aunties and uncles to understand their fear and find a middle ground.
I make cute, emotional posters about loving animals and stick them on the society notice board.
I organize a society meeting, collect a small Rs. 100 fund from each flat, and call a professional NGO.

questions.scenario: You decide to teach the children of your colony's maids and guards in the nearby park. What is your role?

options.text: Sitting on the chatai (mat) with them, distributing notebooks, and physically teaching them the alphabet.
Noticing if a child seems upset or hungry, talking to them gently, and trying to understand their home situation.
Using fun Hindi rhymes, storytelling, and drawing games to make them laugh and learn at the same time.
Talking to their parents to convince them about the value of education and helping them fill out government school admission forms.

questions.scenario: A massive flood hits another state (like Assam or Kerala) and your school is helping. What is your reaction?

options.text: Wishing you could pack your bags, take the train there, and physically distribute rice and blankets on the ground.
Reading deeply about the trauma families are facing and wondering how they will rebuild their lives emotionally.
Singing a heartfelt song or painting an emotional poster to spread awareness and empathy on Instagram.
Taking charge of the school's donation drive, making a list of needed items, and packing boxes efficiently.

questions.scenario: Your neighborhood is organizing a 'Swachh Bharat' Sunday cleanup. What is your approach?

options.text: Wearing gloves, tying a bandana, and getting right into picking up the garbage and clearing the drains.
Observing why people litter in specific corners and talking to the local shopkeepers to change their habits.
Painting beautiful murals of Indian gods or nature on the dirty walls so people stop spitting paan there.
Getting permission from the local corporator (parshad) and ensuring the municipality garbage truck arrives on time.

questions.scenario: You see elderly people (Dadajis and Dadis) sitting alone in the park every evening. What do you do?

options.text: Walking up to them, helping them safely cross the busy road, and carrying their grocery bags home.
Sitting beside them, asking about their childhood, and patiently listening to their stories to cure their loneliness.
Organizing a fun game of Antakshari, Ludo, or singing old Kishore Kumar songs to cheer up the whole group.
Starting a 'Senior Citizens Club' in the society WhatsApp group to plan weekly yoga sessions and health checkups for them.

questions.scenario: Your school group is performing a Nukkad Natak (Street Play) in the local market. What's your role?

options.text: Going shop-to-shop in the hot sun to gather a crowd and handing out awareness pamphlets to the public.
Watching the crowd's facial expressions closely to see if they are actually understanding the deep message.
Acting with intense energy in the lead role, playing the dholak, and shouting the slogans loudly.
Managing the permissions from the local police station and organizing auto-rickshaws for the team's transport.

questions.scenario: Your best friend is going through a massive breakdown because of Class 10 Board Exam pressure. How do you help?

options.text: Physically dragging them out of their room, forcing them to eat golgappas, and going for a long walk to distract them.
Sitting quietly with them, asking deep questions, validating their fears, and calming their anxiety step-by-step.
Drawing a funny comic about their strict math teacher to make them laugh and lighten the heavy mood.
Taking their syllabus, breaking it down into a realistic 30-day timetable, and tracking their daily progress.

questions.scenario: You visit a rural village during your summer vacation. How do you spend your free time?

options.text: Going to the fields to help the farmers or working with local women to fetch water from the handpump.
Having a long chat with the village Sarpanch to deeply understand why the youth are leaving for the city.
Gathering the village kids under a banyan tree and teaching them how to make cool origami crafts.
Figuring out how to connect the village's primary health center with a big hospital in the city for better supplies.

questions.scenario: There is a local Mela (fair) near your house to support poor Indian artisans. How are you involved?

options.text: Helping the potters and weavers physically unpack their heavy boxes and set up their small stalls.
Talking to the artisans about the struggles of their trade and thinking of ways to preserve their livelihood.
Decorating the entrance gate of the mela with colorful dupattas, marigold flowers, and fairy lights.
Handling the main ticket counter, making sure there is enough loose change (chillar), and tracking the daily sales.

questions.scenario: It's Diwali, and you want to do something meaningful for the community instead of just bursting crackers. What do you do?

options.text: Going directly to the nearby slums to hand out boxes of homemade kaju katli and diyas to families.
Spending the evening talking to the security guards or hostel students who couldn't go home for the festival.
Organizing a massive, colorful rangoli competition for all the kids in the neighborhood to bring everyone together.
Collecting old but good condition clothes from 50 houses, sorting them by size, and managing a mass donation drive.

Field_Social_Worker.title: The Ground Crusader (Field Social Worker)
Field_Social_Worker.primary_match_text: You are a woman/man of action! You don't just feel bad about society's problems; you get your hands dirty to fix them. You love being outdoors and interacting with people directly.
Field_Social_Worker.day_in_the_life: Traveling to rural villages or slums, distributing medical supplies, organizing health camps, and making a direct physical impact on people's lives every single day.
Field_Social_Worker.alternative_match_text: Your active nature and desire to help make you perfect for roles like Disaster Relief Worker, Environmental Activist, or Public Health Volunteer.
Field_Social_Worker.roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities/Arts (Sociology or Political Science is helpful). Degree: Bachelor of Social Work (BSW) or BA in Sociology. Next Steps: Pursue a Master of Social Work (MSW) and intern with NGOs like Teach For India or Goonj.

Case_Worker.title: The Mind Healer (Psychologist / Case Worker)
Case_Worker.primary_match_text: You are an incredibly empathetic listener with a sharp, analytical mind. People naturally trust you with their deepest secrets. You want to heal the root cause of trauma.
Case_Worker.day_in_the_life: Sitting in a quiet office or community center, listening to people's struggles, tracking their mental health progress, and creating step-by-step plans to help families recover.
Case_Worker.alternative_match_text: Your deep empathy and analytical skills also make you a fantastic Clinical Psychologist, School Counselor, or Human Rights Researcher.
Case_Worker.roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities/Arts with Psychology. Degree: BA or B.Sc in Psychology. Next Steps: Pursue an MA in Clinical or Counseling Psychology, clear the UGC-NET, and get licensed by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI).

Nukkad_Natak_Educator.title: The Creative Catalyst (Community Arts Educator)
Nukkad_Natak_Educator.primary_match_text: You believe that art can change the world! You are highly creative, expressive, and know how to capture people's attention. You use emotions and culture to teach powerful lessons.
Nukkad_Natak_Educator.day_in_the_life: Writing scripts for street plays, organizing art therapy workshops for underprivileged kids, and using music, dance, and painting to spread awareness on social issues.
Nukkad_Natak_Educator.alternative_match_text: If not in direct social work, your creativity would make you a brilliant Documentary Filmmaker, Drama Teacher, or Creative Director for social campaigns.
Nukkad_Natak_Educator.roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities/Arts (Fine Arts is a plus). Degree: Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA), BA in Performing Arts, or Mass Communication. Next Steps: Combine your degree with a diploma in Art Therapy or work with creative NGOs.

Community_Center_Manager.title: The Impact Leader (NGO Manager / Social Entrepreneur)
Community_Center_Manager.primary_match_text: You are the boss with a big heart! You have an amazing business sense, love organizing things, and know how to manage money and people to create massive social change.
Community_Center_Manager.day_in_the_life: Managing the budget of an NGO, pitching social project ideas to big corporate companies for CSR funding, paying staff salaries, and ensuring the community center runs smoothly.
Community_Center_Manager.alternative_match_text: Your leadership skills would make you an excellent Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Head, Rural Development Officer, or Business Entrepreneur.
Community_Center_Manager.roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Humanities. Degree: BBA, B.Com, or BA. Next Steps: Highly recommended to pursue an MBA in Rural Management (from institutes like IRMA) or a Master's in Public Policy/Social Entrepreneurship.
